title: A beat is a signal, not an outcome.

study.title: A beat is a signal, not an outcome.
study.summary: See the arithmetic of two tones while keeping clinical outcomes outside the oscillator model.

inputs.label: Centre carrier
inputs.meaning: Midpoint of the two generated tones, not a human natural frequency.

inputs.label: Tone separation
inputs.meaning: Difference between component frequencies; no health or brain-state prediction follows.

assumptions: A two-tone monaural demonstration with fixed quiet digital amplitude; not a binaural physiological model.

Waveform is synthetic at 8000 samples/s over 0.25 s. Linear taper lasts min(20 ms, one-quarter of the sample count) at each end; ms means millisecond. Master sample-peak ceiling is -24 dBFS (decibels relative to digital full scale), gain 10^(-24/20); this is not measured sound pressure or a true-peak limit. This page does not play sound.
setup: Inspect generated samples and the documented digital amplitude before any future listening use.
For acoustic measurements, characterize DAC (digital-to-analog converter), amplifier, transducer and microphone separately.
Any clinical question needs a defined intervention, comparator, participant safeguards and a validated clinical outcome; oscillator equations do not supply them.
controls: Matched loudness and expectancy controls in any separate human study.
Compare source arithmetic with acoustic output; digital amplitude is not sound pressure.
study.falsifier: A proposed physiological mechanism must predict a preregistered measured outcome beyond credible sham/expectancy controls; tone arithmetic alone cannot satisfy it.
study.scope: Deterministic audio arithmetic and a graded literature review. No treatment, healing simulation or clinical recommendation.

metrics.label: Tone separation
metrics.meaning: Physical component difference; not a measured brainwave or clinical endpoint.

warnings: The 0.25 s display may show less than one beat cycle.
Digital full scale cannot be converted to dB SPL (sound pressure level) without a calibrated playback chain.

equations.meaning: f1 and f2 are component frequencies; f_c their midpoint, d_f their difference (Hz), t time in seconds. Multiply the two-tone sum by 10^(-24/20)/2 and a linear taper. At sample i, taper=min(1, i/T, (N-1-i)/T), N=2000, T=min(floor(0.02*8000), floor(N/4))=160 samples. Both endpoints are zero. The plot retains every 8000 Hz sample.

defaultCalculation.interpretation: Deterministic audio arithmetic and a graded literature review. No treatment, healing simulation or clinical recommendation.

glossary.Pa: Pascal, pressure equal to one newton per square metre.
glossary.K: Kelvin, the SI unit of temperature; temperature differences of 1K and 1°C have equal size.
glossary.ppm: Parts per million; a relative value multiplied by one million.
glossary.ppb: Parts per billion; a relative value multiplied by one billion.
glossary.RLC: A circuit containing resistance R in ohms, inductance L in henry and capacitance C in farad.
glossary.RMS: Root mean square, a waveform amplitude convention distinct from peak.
glossary.DAC: Digital-to-analog converter, the electronic stage that turns numeric samples into a voltage.
glossary.EEG: Electroencephalography, a measured scalp electrical signal; not simulated here.
glossary.SPL: Sound pressure level, an acoustic measurement requiring calibration.
glossary.GLB: Binary glTF, a 3D scene file format; this file contains illustrative geometry.
glossary.SVG: Scalable Vector Graphics, a vector drawing format.
glossary.OSF: Open Science Framework, the repository hosting the independently retrieved registration.
glossary.TOST: Two one-sided tests, an equivalence-testing method; its margin and uncertainty need a declared plan.
glossary.A: Position or condition A in the named protocol; not an ampere unless explicitly stated.
glossary.B: Position or condition B in the named protocol; not magnetic flux density unless explicitly stated.
glossary.LOC1: The external Sphere location-comparison protocol, with its own registered estimand.

sourceRecords.title: Binaural beats to entrain the brain? A systematic review of the effects of binaural beat stimulation on brain oscillatory activity, and the implications for psychological research and intervention
sourceRecords.readDepth: Abstract, study selection/inclusion criteria, Results overview, Discussion, Limitations and Conclusion read; individual primary trials and supplementary data not independently reanalysed.
sourceRecords.passage: The methodological heterogeneity in this field of study ultimately limits the comparability of research outcomes.
sourceRecords.claim: Fourteen included studies: abstract/discussion summarize five supportive, eight contradictory and one mixed; authors find inconsistent EEG entrainment and cannot pool effect sizes.
sourceRecords.limitations: Review concerns dichotic binaural stimulation and EEG in selected healthy adults, not all music or all treatments; monaural arithmetic cannot establish clinical healing. Results count overlapping support/mixed categories internally, so no vote-count probability or effect estimate is inferred.

sourceRecords.title: Shukla et al. — Effectiveness of Binaural Beats in Reducing Dental Pain and Anxiety among Children and Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis (2025)
sourceRecords.status: Systematic review and meta-analysis; low-certainty clinical evidence
sourceRecords.readDepth: Primary full-text XML retrieved. Abstract, inclusion criteria, Results risk-of-bias/GRADE and comparisons, Discussion limitations and Conclusion read. Individual trials and forest plots not independently reanalysed.
sourceRecords.passage: The level of evidence inferred from this systematic review inferred a low certainty for reduction of dental pain and anxiety using the GRADE approach.
sourceRecords.claim: Nine studies entered qualitative review and six quantitative analysis. Some anxiety comparisons favored binaural beats; dental pain versus no intervention was inconclusive with substantial heterogeneity. The authors report high selection/detection bias and urge caution.
sourceRecords.limitations: A specific dental-procedure evidence base is not universal healing, proof of a unique curative frequency, or a validation of this app. Pre/post change alone does not identify a specific binaural mechanism. EEG entrainment and clinical benefit are distinct outcomes.
sourceRecords.passageConvention: Verbatim words; extracted whitespace normalized. No omitted words in this excerpt.
